_comment: Golden parity fixtures for declared effects: what a tool may do to the world, declared in tools.yaml as `effects: [...]` and read by both runtimes. The vocabulary is `fs.read`, `fs.write`, `net` and `exec:<program>` (a program name of lowercase letters, digits, `_` or `-`). `[]` declares a tool with no effects (an Intent that only expands, a pure lookup). A skill's or toolkit's tool that declares nothing is refused when the bundle loads; core control tools are core's and exempt. Each case loads `tools_yaml` as a registry and then applies the skill-bundle rule; `expected` maps each tool to its effects, sorted, or `error_contains` is a phrase the refusal must carry (the same phrase in both runtimes). Consumed by python/core/tests/test_effects_parity.py and native/crates/knaif-core/tests/effects_parity.rs. WHY: Python enforces declared effects at run time (ctx.exec, ctx.call_tool) and native validates them at load until a native context exists (audit F11); both runtimes must agree on what a declaration means.

cases.name: declared_effects_are_read
cases.tools_yaml:
convert:
  description: Convert a file.
  required_args: [input]
  effects: [fs.write, exec:ffmpeg, fs.read]

cases.name: an_empty_list_declares_no_effects
cases.tools_yaml:
plan_it:
  description: Expand into steps.
  required_args: []
  effects: []

cases.name: a_tool_without_effects_is_refused
cases.tools_yaml:
convert:
  description: Convert a file.
  required_args: [input]

cases.name: effects_must_be_a_list
cases.tools_yaml:
read:
  description: Read.
  required_args: []
  effects: fs.read

cases.name: net_and_several_programs
cases.tools_yaml:
fetch:
  description: Fetch.
  required_args: []
  effects: [net, exec:gs, exec:soffice]
